questions.stem: In a transverse wave, the oscillations are:

options.text: Perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
Circular around the direction of travel
Parallel to the direction of energy transfer
In the same direction as the wave speed

questions.explanation: In transverse waves, the oscillations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction of energy transfer. Examples include light and water waves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a longitudinal wave?
questions.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal wave -- the air particles vibrate back and forth parallel to the direction the wave travels, creating compressions and rarefactions.

questions.stem: In a longitudinal wave, the regions where particles are closest together are called:
questions.explanation: Compressions are the regions in a longitudinal wave where particles are pushed close together. Rarefactions are where particles are spread further apart.

questions.stem: Which type of wave can be polarised?
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarised, because their oscillations can be restricted to a single plane. Longitudinal waves oscillate along the direction of travel and cannot be polarised.
All electromagnetic waves (including light, radio waves, and X-rays) are transverse waves, with oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to the direction of travel.

questions.stem: Which seismic wave type is longitudinal?
questions.explanation: P-waves (primary waves) are longitudinal seismic waves. They travel faster than S-waves (which are transverse) and can pass through liquids and solids.

questions.stem: What is the key difference between transverse and longitudinal waves?

options.text: Transverse waves are faster than longitudinal waves
The direction of oscillation relative to the direction of energy transfer
Transverse waves need a medium but longitudinal waves do not

questions.explanation: The key difference is the direction of oscillation: transverse oscillations are perpendicular to energy transfer, while longitudinal oscillations are parallel to it.
